cards.front: Which cells make gastrin, what triggers its release, and what is its main effect?
cards.back: **G cells** of the gastric antrum and duodenum. Triggers: **peptides and amino acids**, **stomach distention** and **vagal** input. Main effect: more **HCl**, acting on parietal cells and, above all, on **ECL cells** (histamine release). Gastrin is also trophic to the gastric mucosa.
cards.back_pt: **Células G** do antro gástrico e do duodeno. Estímulos: **peptídeos e aminoácidos**, **distensão do estômago** e estímulo **vagal**. Efeito principal: mais **HCl**, atuando nas células parietais e, sobretudo, nas **células ECL** (liberação de histamina). A gastrina também é trófica para a mucosa gástrica.

cards.back: **I cells** of the duodenum and jejunum release CCK in response to **fatty acids and amino acids**. Actions: **gallbladder contraction**, **sphincter of Oddi relaxation**, **pancreatic enzyme secretion**, and **slower gastric emptying**.
cards.back_pt: As **células I** do duodeno e do jejuno liberam CCK em resposta a **ácidos graxos e aminoácidos**. Ações: **contração da vesícula biliar**, **relaxamento do esfíncter de Oddi**, **secreção de enzimas pancreáticas** e **retardo do esvaziamento gástrico**.

cards.front: What releases secretin, and what does secretin do?
cards.back: **S cells** in the duodenum release it when **acid** enters the duodenum. It increases **pancreatic bicarbonate** (and biliary bicarbonate) secretion and **inhibits gastrin release and gastric acid**. The result: the duodenal pH rises so pancreatic enzymes can work.
cards.back_pt: As **células S** do duodeno a liberam quando **ácido** chega ao duodeno. Ela aumenta a secreção de **bicarbonato pancreático** (e biliar) e **inibe a liberação de gastrina e a secreção ácida gástrica**. Resultado: o pH duodenal sobe e as enzimas pancreáticas conseguem atuar.

cards.front: Why does oral glucose cause more insulin release than the same amount of glucose given IV?
cards.back: Oral glucose releases **incretins** from the gut: **GIP** (from **K cells** of the duodenum and jejunum) and GLP-1. GIP **increases insulin release** from beta cells. IV glucose bypasses the gut, so there is no incretin effect.
cards.back_pt: A glicose oral libera **incretinas** do intestino: **GIP** (das **células K** do duodeno e do jejuno) e GLP-1. O GIP **aumenta a liberação de insulina** pelas células beta. A glicose IV não passa pelo intestino, então não há efeito incretina.

cards.front: What is the migrating motor complex (MMC), and which hormone drives it?
cards.back: During **fasting**, waves of strong contraction move from the stomach to the ileum about every 90 minutes and sweep out leftover contents. **Motilin** (from duodenal cells) drives them. **Erythromycin** stimulates motilin receptors and speeds gastric emptying.
cards.back_pt: No **jejum**, ondas de contração forte vão do estômago ao íleo aproximadamente a cada 90 minutos e varrem o conteúdo residual. A **motilina** (de células duodenais) as comanda. A **eritromicina** estimula os receptores de motilina e acelera o esvaziamento gástrico.

cards.front: How do glucose, galactose and fructose enter and leave the enterocyte?
cards.back: Apical entry: **glucose and galactose** by **SGLT1** (Na+-dependent cotransport); **fructose** by **GLUT5** (facilitated diffusion). Basolateral exit: all three by **GLUT2**.
cards.back_pt: Entrada apical: **glicose e galactose** pelo **SGLT1** (cotransporte dependente de Na+); **frutose** pelo **GLUT5** (difusão facilitada). Saída basolateral: os três pelo **GLUT2**.

cards.front: Outline the path of dietary fat from the lumen to the blood.
cards.back: Pancreatic **lipase** makes fatty acids and monoglycerides. **Bile salts** pack them into **micelles**, which deliver them to the enterocyte. Inside, they are rebuilt into triglycerides and packed with **apoB-48** into **chylomicrons**, which enter the **lacteals** (lymph).
cards.back_pt: A **lipase** pancreática gera ácidos graxos e monoglicerídeos. Os **sais biliares** os reúnem em **micelas**, que os levam ao enterócito. Lá dentro, são reesterificados em triglicerídeos e empacotados com **apoB-48** em **quilomícrons**, que entram nos **vasos quilíferos** (linfa).

cards.front: Where are iron, folate, vitamin B12 and bile salts mainly absorbed?
cards.back: **Iron**: **duodenum**. **Folate**: **jejunum**. **Vitamin B12** (bound to intrinsic factor) and **bile salts**: **terminal ileum**.
cards.back_pt: **Ferro**: **duodeno**. **Folato**: **jejuno**. **Vitamina B12** (ligada ao fator intrínseco) e **sais biliares**: **íleo terminal**.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman has had several episodes of steady right upper quadrant pain. Each episode starts about 30 minutes after a meal rich in fat and lasts 1 to 2 hours. Temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F). Between episodes, the abdomen is soft and not tender. Liver enzymes and lipase are normal. Ultrasound shows several gallstones in a thin-walled gallbladder. Release of which hormone, and from which cells, best explains why her pain follows fatty meals?
choices: Secretin from S cells of the duodenum
Gastrin from G cells of the gastric antrum
Cholecystokinin from I cells of the duodenum and jejunum
Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide from K cells of the duodenum
Motilin from enteroendocrine cells of the duodenum
questions.explanation: Fatty acids in the duodenum release **CCK** from **I cells**. CCK makes the **gallbladder contract** while a stone blocks the cystic duct, which causes **biliary colic**. **Secretin** is the tempting choice because it also comes from the duodenum, but its stimulus is acid and its main effect is pancreatic and biliary **bicarbonate** secretion, not gallbladder contraction.
questions.explanation_pt: Ácidos graxos no duodeno liberam **CCK** das **células I**. A CCK faz a **vesícula biliar contrair** enquanto um cálculo obstrui o ducto cístico, o que causa **cólica biliar**. A **secretina** é a alternativa tentadora porque também vem do duodeno, mas seu estímulo é o ácido e seu efeito principal é a secreção de **bicarbonato** pancreático e biliar, não a contração da vesícula.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with Crohn disease had surgical removal of his last 150 cm of ileum because of a stricture. The duodenum and jejunum are normal. He takes no vitamin supplements. Four years later, he has fatigue, paresthesias in both feet, and loose, greasy stools. Hemoglobin is low and the mean corpuscular volume is 112 fL. Which additional laboratory finding is most likely?
choices: Elevated homocysteine with normal methylmalonic acid
questions.explanation: The **terminal ileum** absorbs **vitamin B12** (with intrinsic factor) and **bile salts**. Loss of B12 causes megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy with high **methylmalonic acid and homocysteine**. Loss of bile salts reduces micelle formation, so fecal fat rises and fat-soluble vitamins (such as vitamin D) fall. **Folate** deficiency, the most tempting choice, also gives macrocytosis and high homocysteine, but methylmalonic acid stays normal and folate is absorbed in the intact jejunum.
questions.explanation_pt: O **íleo terminal** absorve a **vitamina B12** (com o fator intrínseco) e os **sais biliares**. A perda de B12 causa anemia megaloblástica e neuropatia, com **ácido metilmalônico e homocisteína** elevados. A perda de sais biliares reduz a formação de micelas, então a gordura fecal aumenta e as vitaminas lipossolúveis (como a vitamina D) caem. A deficiência de **folato**, a alternativa mais tentadora, também causa macrocitose e homocisteína alta, mas o ácido metilmalônico fica normal, e o folato é absorvido no jejuno, que está intacto.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy has chronic diarrhea and poor weight gain since birth. Exam shows generalized edema. Serum albumin is low. Liver enzymes and urinalysis are normal, and a sweat chloride test is normal. Duodenal fluid contains normal amounts of trypsinogen and chymotrypsinogen but almost no trypsin activity. When a small amount of active trypsin is added to the sample, full activity of trypsin, chymotrypsin and carboxypeptidase appears. Deficiency of which enzyme best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes proteases as inactive **zymogens** so they do not digest the pancreas itself. In the duodenum, the brush-border enzyme **enteropeptidase** (enterokinase) turns **trypsinogen into trypsin**, and trypsin then activates the other zymogens. Without enteropeptidase, protein digestion fails, which causes hypoalbuminemia and edema; added trypsin restores the cascade. **Pancreatic lipase** deficiency would cause steatorrhea, but it would not explain the absent protease activity.
questions.explanation_pt: O pâncreas secreta as proteases como **zimogênios** inativos para que não digiram o próprio pâncreas. No duodeno, a enzima da borda em escova **enteropeptidase** (enteroquinase) converte o **tripsinogênio em tripsina**, e a tripsina ativa os outros zimogênios. Sem enteropeptidase, a digestão de proteínas falha, causando hipoalbuminemia e edema; a tripsina adicionada restaura a cascata. A deficiência de **lipase pancreática** causaria esteatorreia, mas não explicaria a falta de atividade das proteases.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old man has had burning retrosternal pain after large meals for 3 months. He has no weight loss, dysphagia or vomiting. He is started on famotidine, and his symptoms improve. This drug blocks the parietal cell response to a paracrine signal. Which cell type releases that signal?
questions.explanation: Famotidine blocks the **H2 receptor** on parietal cells. Its ligand, **histamine**, comes from **ECL cells** next to parietal cells; H2 activation raises **cAMP** and increases **H+/K+-ATPase** activity. **G cells** are the tempting choice because gastrin also stimulates acid, but gastrin is a hormone that acts on CCK-B receptors and mostly works by making ECL cells release histamine.
questions.explanation_pt: A famotidina bloqueia o **receptor H2** das células parietais. Seu ligante, a **histamina**, vem das **células ECL** vizinhas às parietais; a ativação do H2 aumenta o **AMPc** e a atividade da **H+/K+-ATPase**. As **células G** são a alternativa tentadora porque a gastrina também estimula o ácido, mas a gastrina é um hormônio que atua nos receptores CCK-B e age principalmente fazendo as células ECL liberarem histamina.

notes.title: GI physiology: hormones, secretions, absorption and motility
notes.body_md:
## Gastric acid

- Parietal cells secrete H+ through the **H+/K+-ATPase** (proton pump), the final common step.
- Stimulators: **ACh** (vagus, M3), **histamine** (from ECL cells, H2) and **gastrin** (CCK-B).
- Inhibitors: **somatostatin** (D cells, released when the lumen is acidic), **prostaglandins**, and secretin.

## Other hormones

- **CCK** (I cells; fat and amino acids): gallbladder contraction, pancreatic enzymes, slower gastric emptying.
- **Secretin** (S cells; duodenal acid): pancreatic **bicarbonate**, less gastric acid.
- **Somatostatin** brakes almost all GI secretion and hormone release.
- **VIP** relaxes GI smooth muscle and increases intestinal water and chloride secretion. A **VIPoma** causes watery diarrhea, hypokalemia and **achlorhydria**.
- **GIP** raises insulin release after oral glucose.

## Secretions

- **Saliva**: hypotonic, rich in K+ and bicarbonate; contains **alpha-amylase**. Both parasympathetic and sympathetic input increase it.
- **Pancreatic juice**: isotonic; bicarbonate rises and chloride falls as flow rises. Amylase and lipase are active when secreted. Proteases leave as **zymogens**; **enteropeptidase** activates **trypsinogen**, and trypsin activates the rest.
- **Bile acids**: made in the liver from cholesterol (**7-alpha-hydroxylase** is the rate-limiting enzyme) and conjugated with glycine or taurine. Most are reabsorbed in the **terminal ileum** and return to the liver (**enterohepatic circulation**).

## Digestion and absorption

- Brush-border **disaccharidases** (lactase, sucrase, maltase) make monosaccharides.
- Glucose and galactose: **SGLT1**. Fructose: **GLUT5**. Exit: **GLUT2**.
- Fat: micelles, then **chylomicrons** into lymph.
- Iron: duodenum. Folate: jejunum. B12 and bile salts: terminal ileum.

## Motility

- **Interstitial cells of Cajal** make **slow waves**, which set the maximum contraction rate.
- **Peristalsis** moves contents forward; **segmentation** mixes them.
- **Receptive relaxation**: the proximal stomach relaxes as food arrives (vagal reflex).
- The **migrating motor complex** (motilin) clears the gut during fasting.
- A meal in the stomach increases ileal and colonic activity (**gastroileal** and **gastrocolic reflexes**).
- **Defecation**: rectal stretch relaxes the internal anal sphincter; the external sphincter is voluntary.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Ácido gástrico

- As células parietais secretam H+ pela **H+/K+-ATPase** (bomba de prótons), a etapa final comum.
- Estimulantes: **ACh** (vago, M3), **histamina** (das células ECL, H2) e **gastrina** (CCK-B).
- Inibidores: **somatostatina** (células D, liberada quando a luz está ácida), **prostaglandinas** e secretina.

## Outros hormônios

- **CCK** (células I; gordura e aminoácidos): contração da vesícula biliar, enzimas pancreáticas, retardo do esvaziamento gástrico.
- **Secretina** (células S; ácido no duodeno): **bicarbonato** pancreático, menos ácido gástrico.
- A **somatostatina** freia quase toda a secreção e a liberação de hormônios do TGI.
- O **VIP** relaxa o músculo liso do TGI e aumenta a secreção intestinal de água e cloreto. O **VIPoma** causa diarreia aquosa, hipocalemia e **acloridria**.
- O **GIP** aumenta a liberação de insulina após glicose oral.

## Secreções

- **Saliva**: hipotônica, rica em K+ e bicarbonato; contém **alfa-amilase**. Os estímulos parassimpático e simpático a aumentam.
- **Suco pancreático**: isotônico; o bicarbonato sobe e o cloreto cai quando o fluxo aumenta. Amilase e lipase são secretadas ativas. As proteases saem como **zimogênios**; a **enteropeptidase** ativa o **tripsinogênio**, e a tripsina ativa os demais.
- **Ácidos biliares**: produzidos no fígado a partir do colesterol (a **7-alfa-hidroxilase** é a enzima limitante) e conjugados com glicina ou taurina. A maioria é reabsorvida no **íleo terminal** e volta ao fígado (**circulação êntero-hepática**).

## Digestão e absorção

- As **dissacaridases** da borda em escova (lactase, sacarase, maltase) geram monossacarídeos.
- Glicose e galactose: **SGLT1**. Frutose: **GLUT5**. Saída: **GLUT2**.
- Gordura: micelas, depois **quilomícrons** para a linfa.
- Ferro: duodeno. Folato: jejuno. B12 e sais biliares: íleo terminal.

## Motilidade

- As **células intersticiais de Cajal** geram **ondas lentas**, que definem a frequência máxima de contração.
- A **peristalse** empurra o conteúdo; a **segmentação** o mistura.
- **Relaxamento receptivo**: o estômago proximal relaxa quando o alimento chega (reflexo vagal).
- O **complexo motor migratório** (motilina) limpa o intestino no jejum.
- Uma refeição no estômago aumenta a atividade do íleo e do cólon (**reflexos gastroileal** e **gastrocólico**).
- **Defecação**: a distensão retal relaxa o esfíncter anal interno; o externo é voluntário.
